To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children born to mothers who had diabetes mellitus during their pregnancies, i.e. infants of diabetic mothers, display a higher frequency of impaired glucose tolerance in early childhood than healthy children.

the offspring of mothers who have pregestational IDMM or gestational diabetes mellitus have an increased risk for developing impaired glucose tolerance in childhood, and that hyperinsulinemia at birth may be a pathogenetic factor in the development of impaired glucose tolerance.

the offspring of diabetic mothers are prone to develop impaired glucose tolerance, and that the pathogenetic role for this development is played by hyperinsulinism at birth, which may induce insulin resistance in childhood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic consequences of fetal exposure to maternal diabetes mellitus.
the development of the metabolic phenotype of the infant of the diabetic mother

the development of glucose tolerance and insulin secretory function in the offspring of IDDM and gestational diabetic mothers during the first decade of life, in particular with the influence of the fetal and neonatal insulin response on the development of glucose intolerance in childhood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the offspring of diabetic mothers are at risk of developing glucose tolerance abnormalities in childhood.

the offspring of mothers suffering from pregestational insulin dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) during pregnancy have a higher risk of developing impaired glucose tolerance (2h blood glucose > 140 mg/dl) than the children of mothers with gestational diabetes.
the offspring of mothers who develop gestational diabetes are more prone to develop IGT than the children of IDDM-mothers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the offspring of gestational diabetic women show higher stimulated blood glucose and the offspring of pregestational insulin dependent diabetic women show higher fasting insulin and stimulated insulin and higher fasting insulin/glucose and stimulated insulin/glucos ratios than offspring of non-diabetic women.
the offspring of mothers who had gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are not at an increased risk for the development of type 1 diabetes.
children of gestational diabetics are at higher risk for impaired glucose tolerance than children of mothers with IDDM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the offspring of mothers who had diabetes during pregnancy may be at risk for developing metabolic disorders later in life.
the offspring of mothers who have diabetes during pregnancy are more likely to have diabetes later in life.
the offspring of mothers who had diabetes during pregnancy are at risk for developing diabetes.
